description: Reverb 2: the lusher of the two Surge XT reverbs, with fewer digital artefacts

params.text: Delays the signal before it reaches the reverb, up to 2 seconds, and can be tempo-synced.
Changes the apparent size of the simulated room.
Sets how long the tail takes to fall by 60dB, up to 64 seconds.
Changes the complexity of the room, and with it how diffuse the tail is.
Sets how long the reverb takes to reach its peak, and how smeared in time it is.
Adds pitch modulation to the input for a lusher tail.
Sets how much the low frequencies are absorbed.
Sets how much the high frequencies are absorbed.
Scales the side component of the treated signal, from -24dB to +24dB; at the bottom of its range the output is mono.
Blends between the dry signal and the treated signal.
Modulation depth for one of the four modulation inputs into the knob it belongs to; the figure is the shift a plus or minus 10V signal produces.

inputs.text: The left channel of the signal to be treated; with nothing patched to the right input this one is used for both channels.
The right channel of the signal to be treated.
Carries a modulation signal; arm it with its button, then turn a knob to set how far this signal moves that knob.

notes: The name across the top of the display picks a preset: the arrow at each end moves one along the list, and clicking the name opens the whole list. An asterisk marks an edited preset.
The effect is computed a block of samples at a time, which puts a small fixed delay between the inputs and the outputs.
A modulation input does nothing until you press the button above it to arm it and then drag a knob; the drag sets how far that input moves that knob, and a ring on the knob shows the amount.
menu: Re-Initialize Effect — clears the internal state of the effect, so any tail it is holding stops.
Monophonic Stereo Processing — sums the polyphonic channels into a single instance of the effect.
Polyphonic Stereo Processing — runs a separate instance of the effect for each polyphonic channel.
Use Global Style — ties this module's appearance to the setting shared by every Surge XT module, rather than to this module alone.
Skin — sets the panel colouring: Dark, Medium or Light.
Colors — a submenu setting the colour of the Display Area, Knob and Slider Values, Modulations and Power Buttons, and carrying Show Knob Shadows.
Value Displays — a submenu carrying Knob Value Rings, Knob Modulation Animations and Display Modulation Animations.
